record.tranche_reason: The study finds irreducible multi-dimensional representations in language models and tests their causal role, challenging a one-dimensional-only account. It does not test the original toy-model superposition recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE clustering, irreducibility measurements, circular representations, and interventions on those representations. Reported model accuracies on the arithmetic prompts are task checks, not direct measures of feature geometry, so they are not included as rows. Numbers used to select clustering settings or inspect representations are not treated as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own SAE-clustering, irreducibility tests, PCA geometry and causal interventions in GPT-2-small, Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B show multi-dimensional (circular) features. This argues directly that V6's one-dimensional account needs restating. It also gives synthetic evidence that SAE dictionary directions are not canonical for such features (V5). It does not reproduce the toy-model setup (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim the circular features are causally used as the unit of computation in weekday/month arithmetic. They add that the SAE-derived plane may be a more robust feature than their probe, and they question whether individual SAE features are appropriate mediators. They call the evidence for the multi-dimensional superposition hypothesis preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition. It develops statistical tests and SAE clustering for multi-dimensional features in GPT-2 and Mistral, then uses interventions on circular representations in arithmetic tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: For Mistral SAE clustering, changing the similarity threshold τ changes whether the days-of-week cluster appears; changing k has minimal effect. Circular intervention effects vary by layer, with early-layer effects especially strong. Circular representations are visible at many, but not all, layers.
record.problems: The paper describes its results as preliminary. Irreducibility is defined statistically, with practical relaxed indices, rather than through interventions. The authors manually inspected many clusters and say it is unclear why they found few other interpretable multi-dimensional features. The clustering result depends on a threshold, and some intervention values are presented only in figures.

untested.parts: All of it: toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, the sparsity transition, and regular geometry (Appendix A gives only a theoretical capacity bound).
All of it: capacity competition as the cause of neuron polysemanticity.
Whether features are spread across many neurons; how generally SAEs recover features beyond the selected circular clusters.
Completeness and stability of real-model SAE features; canonicality is tested only on synthetic circle data.
How prevalent multi-dimensional features are; the authors found few beyond days, months and years.

missing.what: Off-distribution interventions over (r, θ) show Mistral encodes α in the circle's angle, so the feature is used as a 2-D representation
Continuity: 'very early/very late' and 'morning/evening' day variants fall between adjacent weekdays on the circle in Mistral layer 30
Ranking of the GPT-2 day, month and year clusters among 1000 clusters by irreducibility score (ranks 9, 28, 15; 8, 105, 12 under an alternative ranking)
Rarity: after manually inspecting about 500 GPT-2 and about 2000 Mistral clusters, few other clearly irreducible interpretable features were found. This qualifies how far the challenge to V6 extends
EVR residuals reveal a circle in γ on the final token (Mistral layer 25 Weekdays; Llama Months)
Synthetic two-circle SAE: alive features align with the two planes and clustering recovers both circles. A 2-D feature is split across many dictionary elements rather than one

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The V4 links on R1–R5 were removed because a single row state cannot be both observed (V4) and reversed (V6); those rows do also show SAEs recovering interpretable structure, as clusters. The record's limits_scope label for R8–R11 was replaced with challenges: the drop-off at layers 15–17 is explained by α being copied to the final token, which does not qualify the effect. R14 is a check on the method's own robustness and was unlinked. The authors report that few multi-dimensional features were found; this tempers how broadly V6 is challenged and is logged under missing.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks storing more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, regular geometry under superposition, or interference from overlapping features.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Tests SAE recovery of selected multi-dimensional features, not whether features generally spread across many neurons.
Tests canonicality in a synthetic circle SAE and reports clustering sensitivity; does not establish completeness or stability of SAE features generally in real models.
Tests selected circular representations and their role in weekday/month arithmetic, not whether all model features are multi-dimensional.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on the weekdays plane found by SAE clustering using an SAE-trained circular probe.
rows.baseline: Layer 8 circular probe: -2.58 on layer 8; 0.029 on layer 6
rows.value: -2.01 on layer 8; -2.32 on layer 6 using the layer 8 SAE probe
rows.note: The paper says the SAE probe only slightly decreases performance versus the per-layer circular probe and is more robust to layer shifts. The intervention results support use of an SAE-recovered multi-dimensional feature, not a general claim that SAE features are complete or canonical.
rows.check: This is partly a comparison of the authors' own probe methods. The 'baseline' field mixes the per-layer probe (-2.58 at layer 8) with the layer-8 circular probe applied at layer 6 (0.029). The bearing on V4 is that a plane recovered from SAE clusters is causally used.
